questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 2: Dissolving Effervescent Tablets
Students tested how water temperature affects the time required for identical effervescent tablets to stop producing visible bubbles. In Experiment 1, they used 200 mL of water at four temperatures and one whole tablet per trial. In Experiment 2, they repeated the test with crushed tablets while keeping the water volume and temperatures unchanged.

Which follow-up would most directly strengthen or extend the investigation?
A) Repeat only the result that best matches the original expectation and discard the others.
B) Repeat trials at each condition to estimate variation and reduce the influence of an unusual tablet.
C) Change every variable at once so that no control condition remains.
D) Stop collecting measurements and infer the answer from the graph title.

options.A: Repeat only the result that best matches the original expectation and discard the others.
options.B: Repeat trials at each condition to estimate variation and reduce the influence of an unusual tablet.
options.C: Change every variable at once so that no control condition remains.
options.D: Stop collecting measurements and infer the answer from the graph title.

questions.explanation: The proposed follow-up changes or replicates conditions in a way that produces interpretable additional evidence.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 5: Salt-Tolerant Seed Coatings
Researchers evaluated a biodegradable coating intended to improve germination in salty soil. Equal groups of seeds received no coating, a thin coating, or a thick coating. Each group was planted in soil with the same salt concentration, temperature, light, and water. The percentage germinated after 7 days and mean root length of germinated seeds were recorded.

Which conclusion is best supported by the combined experiments?
F) The experiment proves the pattern will remain unchanged under every possible condition.
G) The independent variable had no relationship to any measured outcome.
H) The thin coating produced the highest germination and longest roots among the tested treatments.
J) The data justify replacing all observations with a single average.

options.A: The experiment proves the pattern will remain unchanged under every possible condition.
options.B: The independent variable had no relationship to any measured outcome.
options.C: The thin coating produced the highest germination and longest roots among the tested treatments.
options.D: The data justify replacing all observations with a single average.

questions.explanation: The conclusion reflects the measured results and remains within the experimental scope.

questions.stem:
SCIENCE PASSAGE 5: Protective Coatings and Corrosion
Steel washers were cleaned, weighed, and coated with no coating, wax, paint, or a plant-based film. The washers were placed in equal volumes of saltwater for 10 days, dried, and reweighed. Greater mass loss indicates more corrosion. A second observation recorded the percentage of each surface covered by rust.

Which conclusion is best supported by the combined experiments?
F) The experiment proves the pattern will remain unchanged under every possible condition.
G) The independent variable had no relationship to any measured outcome.
H) Paint provided the greatest protection in both measured outcomes, and the plant film reduced corrosion relative to no coating.
J) The data justify replacing all observations with a single average.

options.A: The experiment proves the pattern will remain unchanged under every possible condition.
options.B: The independent variable had no relationship to any measured outcome.
options.C: Paint provided the greatest protection in both measured outcomes, and the plant film reduced corrosion relative to no coating.
options.D: The data justify replacing all observations with a single average.

questions.explanation: The conclusion reflects the measured results and remains within the experimental scope.

SCIENCE MATERIAL SET 30
Students tested how water temperature affected the time required for a tablet to dissolve. They used identical tablets, 129 mL of water in each cup, and stirred each cup at the same rate.

TABLE 1
Temperature (°C) | Dissolving time (s)
10 | 33
20 | 25
30 | 20
40 | 16

Trial 2 repeated the procedure with twice the water volume. Researcher 1 claims that higher temperature increases particle motion and therefore decreases dissolving time. Researcher 2 agrees that temperature matters but claims that stirring rate is the dominant factor whenever stirring is not controlled.

Which mechanism best explains the Table 1 trend?
A) Warmer water increases particle motion and collision frequency.
B) Warmer water stops all molecular motion.
C) Temperature removes the tablet before timing begins.
D) The stopwatch changes the water volume.

options.A: Warmer water increases particle motion and collision frequency.
options.B: Warmer water stops all molecular motion.
options.C: Temperature removes the tablet before timing begins.
options.D: The stopwatch changes the water volume.
